We investigate how qualitative advantages of LLMs change when fine-tuning on parallel data. We consider LLaMA and Falcon models, with parameter counts ranging from 7 billion up to 65 billion. The LLM properties we investigate are general translation quality, formality steerability, non-literalness in idiom translations, performance on specialized domains, and performance on document-level input which requires contextualisation of ambiguous tokens.
